# LLM fundamentals

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/llm-fundamentals.md) · [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md) › [Themes](../README.md#themes)

How transformers and LLMs work: attention, tokens, context, sampling, scaling. Engineers derive and implement; leaders need the intuition behind cost, quality and limits.

On this page: [Both tracks (2)](#track-both) · [AI Engineering (16)](#track-engineering)

## <a id="track-both"></a>Both tracks

- <a id="llm-compute-optimal"></a>**Under a fixed training compute budget, how do Chinchilla-style scaling results change the balance between model size and training tokens?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) † · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#llm-compute-optimal) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-compute-optimal&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-compute-optimal)
  - Tests: Whether empirical training trade-offs are kept separate from deployment economics.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - State the fixed-compute setting and the empirical nature of the fit.
    - Balance parameter count with sufficient training tokens.
    - Separate training-optimal allocation from inference cost and data quality constraints.
  - Read: [Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556) (Hoffmann et al., arXiv)
- <a id="llm-training-stages"></a>**What objectives and data distinguish pretraining, instruction tuning and preference optimisation?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) † · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-training-stages&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-training-stages)
  - Tests: Whether the candidate can identify what each stage can and cannot change.

## <a id="track-engineering"></a>AI Engineering

- <a id="llm-attention"></a>**Derive scaled dot-product attention and explain how its scale affects softmax gradients.**
  - Knowledge · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#llm-attention) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-attention&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-attention)
  - Tests: Whether tensor shapes and numerical behaviour support the explanation.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Track Q, K and V shapes through score computation and weighted summation.
    - Scale by the square root of key width; discuss saturation of softmax.
    - Apply the causal mask before softmax and check numerical stability.
  - Read: [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) (Vaswani et al., arXiv)
- <a id="llm-kv-cache"></a>**Derive the memory required by a decoder's KV cache as batch size and context length grow.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Amazon](../companies/amazon.md) †, [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) † · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#llm-kv-cache) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-kv-cache&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-kv-cache)
  - Tests: Whether cache size is calculated from the actual architecture.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - For equal sequence lengths, use 2 × batch × layers × tokens × KV heads × head width × bytes.
    - Explain why queries are not retained for future decode steps.
    - Account separately for weights, activations, padding and allocation overhead.
  - Read: [Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180) (Kwon et al., arXiv) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245) (Ainslie et al., arXiv)
- <a id="llm-grouped-query"></a>**Compare multi-head, multi-query and grouped-query attention in quality and serving memory.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) † · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#llm-grouped-query) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-grouped-query&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-grouped-query)
  - Tests: Whether shared keys and values are distinguished from query heads.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - MHA uses separate KV heads; MQA shares one; GQA shares within groups.
    - Relate KV-head count to cache size and memory reads.
    - Discuss quality evaluation and the need to train or adapt the checkpoint.
  - Read: [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245) (Ainslie et al., arXiv)
- <a id="llm-latent-attention"></a>**Explain how latent attention compresses the KV representation and what must be reconstructed at inference.**
  - Knowledge · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#llm-latent-attention) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-latent-attention&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-latent-attention)
  - Tests: Whether architectural compression is distinguished from lower numeric precision.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Cache one low-rank latent vector per token instead of full keys and values for every head.
    - Reconstruct per-head keys and values from that latent during attention, paying extra compute.
    - Separate this architectural compression from quantising the same cache.
  - Read: [DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04434) (DeepSeek-AI, arXiv)
- <a id="llm-flashattention"></a>**Why can an exact attention kernel run faster without changing the quadratic attention computation?**
  - Knowledge · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-flashattention&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-flashattention)
  - Tests: Whether memory traffic is separated from arithmetic complexity.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Explain tiled attention and the reduction in reads and writes between accelerator memory levels.
    - Distinguish exact attention with floating-point differences from sparse or approximate attention.
    - Separate quadratic arithmetic from memory traffic; benchmark the relevant shapes and hardware.
  - Read: [FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135) (Dao et al., arXiv)

- <a id="llm-experts"></a>**How does sparse expert routing increase parameter capacity, and what costs remain despite activating only some experts?**
  - Knowledge · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#llm-experts) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-experts&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-experts)
  - Tests: Whether active computation, total memory and communication are separated.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Separate the total parameter count from the parameters activated for one token.
    - Account for memory that must hold every expert and for routing traffic between devices.
    - Discuss load imbalance, expert capacity and dropped tokens.

- <a id="llm-context-position"></a>**How would you test and reduce a model's tendency to miss relevant evidence in the middle of a long context?**
  - Knowledge · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#llm-context-position) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=llm-context-position&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20llm-context-position)
  - Tests: Whether context utilisation is measured rather than inferred from context capacity.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Move the same relevant evidence through controlled context positions.
    - Measure accuracy across lengths, distractors and model variants.
    - Compare retrieval, ordering and context reduction without assuming a universal cure.
  - Read: [Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172) (Liu et al., arXiv)
